answer_value: Only I and III conclusion follow
steps: Some cups are glasses; no glass is a stone; all stones are metals
I: the cups that are glasses are not stones, so all cups cannot be stones: follows
II: cups may be metals, so II does not follow
III: stones are metals and not glasses, so all metals cannot be glasses: follows
check_code:
from itertools import product
regions=[r for r in product([0,1],repeat=4) if any(r)]  # (cup, glass, stone, metal)
I=II=III=True
models=0
for mask in range(1<<len(regions)):
    ne=[regions[i] for i in range(len(regions)) if mask>>i&1]
    if not any(r[0] and r[1] for r in ne): continue
    if any(r[1] and r[2] for r in ne): continue
    if any(r[2] and not r[3] for r in ne): continue
    if not any(r[2] for r in ne): continue  # stones exist
    models+=1
    if all(r[2] for r in ne if r[0]): I=False
    if any(r[0] and r[3] for r in ne): II=False
    if all(r[1] for r in ne if r[3]): III=False
res=(I,II,III)
opts={'A':(False,True,True),'B':(True,False,True),'C':(True,False,False),'D':(True,True,True)}
fit=[k for k,v in opts.items() if v==res]
assert models>0 and fit==['B']
